mutations.name: answer-without-wait-group
mutations.why: the core answers when the handler returned although a git it started is still alive: the lock moves on beside it

mutations.name: effect-settles-at-timeout
mutations.why: the step's tracked effect is the call, which settles when main stops waiting, not when the core is done

mutations.name: next-ignores-the-hold
mutations.why: the chain starts the next holder after a stop without waiting for what the stopped step had in flight

mutations.name: settle-before-group-gone
mutations.why: main settles what waited on a dead core at its close, before the gits of its group are gone: the next holder runs beside them

mutations.name: spawn-ignores-cancel
mutations.why: run.rs starts a git although its request was cancelled
mutations.search: /\ coreUp /\ handler = "running" /\ ~cancelled /\ gits < MaxGits /\ alive < Par
mutations.replace: /\ coreUp /\ handler = "running" /\ gits < MaxGits /\ alive < Par

mutations.name: cancel-never-read
mutations.why: the core skips a cancel frame, so a stopped request runs all its gits; the lock still waits, so only the cancel's own property sees it

mutations.name: stop-without-cancel
mutations.why: a stopped step leaves its request running in the core (2b's read): its git finishes the write instead of being ended
mutations.search: /\ toCore' = IF req = "pending" /\ coreUp THEN Append(toCore, "cancel") ELSE toCore

mutations.name: no-fairness
mutations.why: nothing forces the core to read, answer or the gits to end: a stopped holder could keep the lock forever

mutations.name: answer-while-handler-runs
mutations.why: the core answers before its handler returned

mutations.name: spawn-counts-twice
mutations.why: a spawn counts two live gits, past the range TypeOK states

mutations.name: scratch-outlives-handler
mutations.why: the scratch store is removed after the handler returned (or never): the core answers and the lock moves on while the stopped request's folder is still on disk

mutations.name: answer-before-disk-call-returns
mutations.why: the core answers while a file system call of the request (an archive copy, a removal) still runs on its worker: the lock moves on and that call lands beside the next holder

mutations.name: disk-call-ignores-cancel
mutations.why: a cancelled request goes on copying, removing or walking: a stopped save keeps writing its archive or removing files
